evidence.note: Agent explicitly enumerates the major subsystems (workbook model/persistence, formula evaluator, API routes, import/export, SPA) and states an ordered build sequence: 'model/persistence helpers first, then formula evaluation, API routes, and the SPA' — a dependency-sensible decomposition with foundational pieces first.

Builds each subsystem in the declared order (persistence → parser/evaluator → function catalog → workbook operations → import/export/routes → SPA), but as one continuous linear scaffold with no verification between pieces — the whole package is written before the first test run.
Uses a test subset as a deliberate done-signal: runs API and engine tests first 'because they catch most parser and response-shape issues quickly' — a milestone tied to a specific slice of the suite.

In the fix phase, progressively advances through test slices as milestones: core API/formula corpus green, then the remaining visible suite (anticipating spills/OOXML/collaboration failures), then the full suite 131/131 as the final done-signal. Ordering is coherent but the plan is narrated in prose, never held as an explicit maintained checklist (no TodoWrite).

reasoning: The agent clearly identifies the major subsystems and tackles them in a sensible dependency order with foundational pieces (model/persistence) before dependent ones (routes, SPA), and it ties completion to concrete test-subset done-signals during the debugging phase (engine tests first, then remainder, then full suite) — comfortably above the flat/vague level 3 and meeting level 5. It falls short of level 8 because the milestone plan lives only in narration rather than as an explicit maintained artifact, and construction was one large unverified lump (all subsystems written before any per-milestone check), so milestones were not independently checked as they were built. This places the behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.
